findings.title: Working-hours check uses the slot start time as its end time
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, exactly like `start`. The check therefore never compares the slot's real end (`slotEndTime`) against `workingHour.endTime`. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is treated as available, so meetings can be booked that overrun a fixed host's working hours.

findings.title: Split working hours reject valid slots
findings.body: `workingHours.find` returns true as soon as any working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot, and that makes the slot unavailable. If a host has several ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17, or ranges split at the UTC day boundary), a slot inside 9-12 lies outside 13-17 and gets rejected. The fix is to reject only when the slot falls outside all applicable ranges (use `some`/`every` correctly). As written, fixed and round-robin hosts with multiple ranges lose valid slots.

findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on one day reject slots inside later ranges
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true, meaning 'not available', for the first same-day override whose range does not contain the slot. If a user has two override ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-10 and 14-16), a slot at 14:00 is rejected because it falls outside 9-10, even though it fits the second range. The slot should be accepted if any override range for that day contains it.

findings.title: Override end boundary compares slot start instead of slot end
findings.body: The slot is rejected only when `slotStartTime` is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override ends but runs past it (e.g. a 60-minute slot at 10:30 with an override ending at 11:00) passes the check. The fixed host is then booked outside their overridden availability. The check should compare `slotEndTime` against the override end.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===` (always false)
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so the condition is never true. Zero-length overrides, which mark the user unavailable all day, are not handled by this branch. A slot that straddles the zero-length point then passes the later checks. Use `.isSame()` here.

findings.title: Override day matching mixes shifted organizer time with UTC slot date
findings.body: The override start is shifted by the negated organizer offset and formatted as a date. That date is then compared with the slot's UTC calendar date (`slotStartTime` is `.utc()`). For organizers far from UTC, the organizer's local override day and the slot's UTC day differ near midnight. As a result, overrides can be ignored for slots on the override day, or applied to slots on an adjacent day.

findings.title: Offset-shifted override can wrap past midnight and produce an invalid range
findings.body: Start and end are computed as hour*60+minute after adding the timezone offset. When the shift crosses midnight (e.g. an override ending 22:00 shifted by +3h becomes 01:00), `endTime` ends up smaller than `startTime`. `buildSlots` skips such ranges (`start >= end`), so the override silently yields no slots. Meanwhile it has still removed the user's working hours for that day. The `activeOverrides` filter also uses the unshifted UTC start, so it can choose the wrong invitee day.

findings.title: Parsing Date.toString() output with dayjs is non-standard
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses the locale-style `Date.prototype.toString()` string, which is not ISO 8601. That depends on engine-specific `Date` parsing and drops milliseconds. `override.start` is already a `Date` and should be passed directly.

findings.title: Round-robin fixed-host override fix is not tested
findings.body: The PR's main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides restrict round-robin availability, but no test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host that has an override. The added test only covers a personal event in a second timezone. The existing `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher also does not check the slot count, so missing expected slots go undetected. None of the new `checkIfIsAvailable` paths are covered: multiple ranges, slots running past the override end, and zero-length overrides.
